interpretation.get: Ten typed identities/occurrences assign the selected pointer-field value into an automatic pointer local using retained RTL assignment, then return that local. No body calls.
interpretation.assertion: Twelve typed identities/occurrences retain if(selected bfk_expect(cast Boolean argument, typed integer zero)), whose then body calls an unavailable declaration, followed by return. The builtin and application declaration are distinct dependencies; neither is a name-based native binding or silently omitted guard.
interpretation.baseArrow: Eleven typed identities/occurrences retain an empty statement, RTL assignment of selected _M_get call into an automatic pointer local and return. The defined _M_get body is untraversed.
interpretation.selection: Actual direct targets are reproduced from the saved tail path, not prior locators. Parent pointer initializer reciprocity, const pointer-object wrapper, declared/returned pointer aliases, source/execution parameter-symbol wrappers and retained then/else contexts remain separate facts. Parent arrow call keeps both evaluation flags false; selected calls are LTR.
interpretation.partial: All three selected bodies finish before the related-type 64 bound is reached. The trace exits 3, overall traceComplete=false with one bound issue. No type-bound increase or recursive helper/layout run is used to force completion.
interpretation.unresolved: bfk_expect needs an explicit selected implementation, ThrowNullSharedPtrDereference remains declaration-only with nullable noexcept, and _M_get remains a defined but untraversed direct target. Ordinary nonvirtual pointer-return/local/branch/argument and actual field/base-view storage obligations remain product gaps.

limits: Three selected bodies only: 64 identities/256 occurrences/depth 32 each, combined 16 one-hop dependencies/64 shallow types. Selector identity inventories and call facets do not add body execution or schedule.
